title: Parcial 1 · Unidades 1–4
intro_es: Evalúa el alfabeto y el deletreo, los saludos, el verbo to be, los posesivos, los números, la puntuación, this/that/these/those y las preguntas con WH. Incluye escucha, lectura, escritura y expresión oral.

grammar.q: My sister ___ a nurse.
grammar.explain_es: Con she (my sister) el verbo to be es is.

grammar.q: ___ are my keys. (aquí, en mi mano)
grammar.explain_es: Cerca y plural (keys) → these.

grammar.q: Pedro and Lucía are here with ___ dog.
grammar.explain_es: Hay dos dueños (Pedro y Lucía) → their.

grammar.q: ___ is your birthday? — On the fifth of June.
grammar.explain_es: La respuesta es una fecha (un momento) → When.

grammar.q: Is your teacher from Cali? — No, she ___.
grammar.explain_es: Respuesta corta negativa con she: No, she isn't.

grammar.q: This bag is Laura's. It's ___.
grammar.explain_es: Sin sustantivo después usamos el pronombre posesivo hers (el suyo, de ella).

grammar.q: We ___ from Medellín. (be)
grammar.explain_es: Con we el verbo to be es are.

grammar.q: Make a question: You are a student.
grammar.explain_es: En la pregunta de sí/no, are va antes del sujeto: Are you…?

grammar.q: That shoes are very nice.
grammar.explain_es: Shoes es plural; lejos y plural → those.

grammar.q: your / where / parents / are / ?
grammar.explain_es: Palabra WH + are + sujeto (your parents).

options: capital B – E – double L – A
capital B – I – double L – A
vocabulary.explain_es: Bella empieza con mayúscula (capital B) y tiene dos L seguidas (double L). La E se dice «i».

vocabulary.q: It is 8:00 p.m. You arrive at a party. You say: «___!»
vocabulary.explain_es: Para saludar en la noche usamos Good evening. Good night es para despedirse.
La respuesta natural a Nice to meet you es Nice to meet you, too.
Ochenta = eighty, con una sola T.

vocabulary.q: December is the ___ month of the year.
vocabulary.explain_es: Diciembre es el mes número 12 → ordinal twelfth (twelve → twelfth).
En los correos, @ se dice at: ana at gmail dot com.
J se pronuncia /dʒeɪ/ («yei»). G se dice «yi».
See you tomorrow = hasta mañana.
How are you? pregunta cómo estás → Fine, thanks.
15 = fifteen. El símbolo $ se escribe antes, pero se dice después: fifteen dollars.

reading.title: My Best Friend and Me
paragraphs: Hi! My name is Valeria Ríos. I am fifteen years old and I am from Pereira. My email is vale.rios@mail.com.

This is my best friend, Tomás. His family is from Tunja, but they are in Pereira now. Their house is on Fifth Street, number 48. Tomás is fourteen. His birthday is on the second of March. My birthday is on the twenty-first of May.
Our English teacher is Mr. Cole. He is from Canada. Is he nice? Yes, he is!

questions.explain_es: Falso. El texto dice: «I am from Pereira». La familia de Tomás es de Tunja.
El texto dice: «Tomás is fourteen». Fifteen es la edad de Valeria.

questions.q: Tomás's birthday is on the second of ___.
questions.explain_es: El texto dice: «His birthday is on the second of March».
El texto dice: «He is from Canada».

questions.q: Tomás's family is in Pereira now.
questions.explain_es: Verdadero. El texto dice: «they are in Pereira now».

questions.q: Their house is number ___ on Fifth Street.
questions.explain_es: El texto dice: «Their house is on Fifth Street, number 48».

lines.text: Good morning. What is your name, please?
Good morning. My name is Diego Arango.
How do you spell your last name?
A, R, A, N, G, O. Arango.
Thank you. How old are you, Diego?
I am sixteen.
And what is your phone number?
It is three one five, two two four, zero nine seven six.

questions.q: What time of day is it?
questions.explain_es: Los dos dicen «Good morning», así que es por la mañana.
Diego dice: «My name is Diego Arango» y lo deletrea: A, R, A, N, G, O.

questions.q: The woman asks for Diego's email.
questions.explain_es: Falso. Ella pregunta: «what is your phone number?», no el correo.
Diego dice: «It is three one five, two two four…».
Verdadero. Ella pregunta «How do you spell your last name?» y él dice «A, R, A, N, G, O».

writing.prompt: Write a short message to your new English teacher. Say hello, give your name and spell it, and say how old you are, where you are from and when your birthday is.
writing.prompt_es: Escribe un mensaje corto a tu nuevo profesor: saluda, di tu nombre y deletréalo, tu edad, de dónde eres y tu cumpleaños.
criteria: Start with a greeting (Hello / Hi / Good morning) and end with a farewell (See you…).
Use the verb be: I am / I'm, My name is…
Use possessive adjectives: my name, my birthday.
Write a number or a date in words (fifteen, the ninth of April).
writing.model: Good morning, Ms. Grant! My name is Sara Ortiz, S-A-R-A. I am fifteen years old and I am from Ibagué. My birthday is on the ninth of April. See you on Monday!

prompts.text: Introduce yourself. Say your name and spell it. Then say how old you are and where you are from.
prompts.text_es: Preséntate: di tu nombre y deletréalo, tu edad y de dónde eres.

prompts.text: Look around you. Point at four things, near and far, and say what they are with this, that, these and those.
prompts.text_es: Mira a tu alrededor y señala cuatro cosas, cerca y lejos, usando this, that, these y those.

prompts.text: Role-play: you meet a new classmate. Say hello, ask three questions with What, Where and How old, and say goodbye.
prompts.text_es: Juego de roles: conoces a un compañero nuevo. Salúdalo, hazle tres preguntas (What, Where, How old) y despídete.
tips: What is your name? Where are you from? How old are you?

title: Parcial final · Nivel Pre-A1
intro_es: Evalúa todo el nivel Pre-A1: alfabeto, saludos, to be, posesivos, números, puntuación, demostrativos, preguntas WH, la ropa, el posesivo 's y whose. Incluye escucha, lectura, escritura y expresión oral.

grammar.q: ___ you ready? — Yes, we are.
grammar.explain_es: La respuesta es «we are», así que la pregunta usa Are.

grammar.q: Whose jacket is this? — It's ___.
grammar.explain_es: Para decir de quién es algo usamos dueño + 's: Camilo's.

grammar.q: ___ umbrella is this? — It's mine.
grammar.explain_es: Whose = de quién. Who's significa who is.

grammar.q: My two daughters share a room. The ___ bedroom is very big.
grammar.explain_es: Plural regular terminado en -s: solo se añade el apóstrofo → daughters'.

grammar.q: What is Andrés wearing? — He ___ a blue shirt.
grammar.explain_es: He → is wearing (be + wearing).

grammar.q: Look at that house over there. ___ door is red.
grammar.explain_es: La casa es «it»; su posesivo es its, sin apóstrofo. It's = it is.

grammar.q: ___ flowers over there are beautiful.
grammar.explain_es: Lejos (over there) y plural (flowers) → those.

grammar.q: How ___ is the jacket? — It's thirty dollars.
grammar.explain_es: Para preguntar el precio usamos How much…?

grammar.q: My brother and I are students. ___ school is in Cali.
grammar.explain_es: My brother and I = we → our.

grammar.q: They ___ from Peru. They're from Ecuador.
grammar.explain_es: Negativo de they are → they aren't.

grammar.q: The ___ toys are on the floor. (the children)
grammar.explain_es: Children es un plural irregular (no termina en -s) → children's.

grammar.q: Make it negative: He is at home.
grammar.explain_es: Para el negativo añadimos not después de is: He is not / isn't.

grammar.q: This is the car of my father.
grammar.explain_es: Con personas usamos dueño + 's + cosa: my father's car.

grammar.q: these / whose / are / shoes / ?
grammar.explain_es: Whose + cosa + are + these?

grammar.q: I ___ a student.
grammar.explain_es: Con «I» se usa «am».

grammar.q: She ___ my sister.
grammar.explain_es: Con he/she/it se usa «is».

grammar.q: ___ is my friend Carlos. (he is here, next to me)
grammar.explain_es: «This» para una persona o cosa cercana.

grammar.q: We are from Colombia. ___ country is beautiful.
grammar.explain_es: «Our» es el posesivo de «we».

grammar.q: ___ old are you? — I am twelve.
grammar.explain_es: La edad se pregunta con «How old».

grammar.q: Is he a doctor? — No, he ___.
grammar.explain_es: Respuesta corta negativa con «he»: «he isn't».

grammar.q: ___ shoes are black. (the shoes of Ana)
grammar.explain_es: El posesivo se forma con 's: «Ana's shoes».

grammar.q: They ___ happy today. (to be)
grammar.explain_es: Con «they» se usa «are».

grammar.q: Make it negative (short form): It is cold. → It ___ cold.
grammar.explain_es: Negativo de «is»: «isn't».

grammar.q: What is ___ name? — Her name is Laura.
grammar.explain_es: «Her» es el posesivo de «she».

grammar.q: from / where / you / are / ?
grammar.explain_es: Pregunta: Where + are + you + from?

vocabulary.q: You wear these on your feet when you run.
vocabulary.explain_es: Sneakers (tenis) van en los pies.
Pants (EE. UU.) = trousers (Reino Unido).

vocabulary.q: It's very cold. Put on your ___ and your gloves.
vocabulary.explain_es: Con frío nos ponemos un coat (abrigo).
Las palabras que terminan en -ss forman el plural con -es: dresses.

vocabulary.q: You see your boss at 3:00 p.m. You say: «___»
vocabulary.explain_es: De 12:00 m. a 6:00 p. m. decimos Good afternoon.
? = question mark (signo de interrogación). En inglés solo va al final.
En inglés el pronombre I y los nombres de países van siempre con mayúscula.
El ordinal de three es irregular: third.

vocabulary.q: How do you say the year 2005?
vocabulary.explain_es: Los años 2000–2009 se dicen two thousand (and) five.

vocabulary.q: Have a nice ___! (que tengas un buen día)
vocabulary.explain_es: Have a nice day! es una despedida amable.
Pencil (lápiz) no es ropa; skirt, belt y socks sí.
Sweater (EE. UU.) = jumper (Reino Unido).
Si el verbo termina en -e muda, quitamos la e: writing.
Hello tiene dos L seguidas (double L); la E se dice «i».
15 = fifteen; 50 = fifty.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday…

vocabulary.q: You wear a ___ on your head.
vocabulary.explain_es: «Hat» = sombrero.
Por la mañana: «Good morning».

vocabulary.q: The colour of the sky on a sunny day is ___.
vocabulary.explain_es: El cielo es azul: «blue».

vocabulary.q: The first month of the year is ___.
vocabulary.explain_es: January = enero.
Plural regular: se añade -s.
A, B, C…
Por la tarde-noche: «Good evening».
A «Thank you» se responde «You're welcome».

reading.title: The Lost and Found Box
paragraphs: ## Part 1 · The Lost and Found Box
It is Monday, the third of October, and it is cold in Bogotá. Our teacher, Ms. Peña, is at her desk with a big box. «Whose things are these?» she asks.
Four things are in the box: a green scarf, two black gloves, a red cap and a white sweater. The scarf is Martín's. The gloves are the twins', Lina and Laura. The red cap is mine!
«Whose sweater is this?» Ms. Peña asks. The name on it is J. Ruiz. Julián Ruiz is not here today. He is at home. Is he sick? Maybe.
This is a photo of my family. My name is Daniel and I am ten years old. We are from Medellín.
This is my mother. Her name is Gloria. She is a nurse. That is my father, Ernesto. He is forty-two and he is a bus driver.
These are my sisters, Sara and Valentina. They are twins! Their dresses are yellow. My dog is in the photo too. Its name is Coco and it is brown.
Today is Sunday, the ninth of May. It is our mother’s birthday. We are very happy.
## Part 3 · A Note on the Classroom Door
Hello, students! Welcome to Room 12. I am your new English teacher. My name is Mr. Rojas.
Your books are on the table. The blue books are for Class A and the red books are for Class B. Your pencils are in the box.
The class is on Tuesday and Thursday at eight o’clock. The price of the book is fifteen dollars. See you tomorrow!

questions.explain_es: El texto dice: «It is Monday, the third of October».

questions.q: It is hot in Bogotá today.
questions.explain_es: Falso. El texto dice: «it is cold in Bogotá».
El texto dice: «The scarf is Martín's».
El texto dice: «The gloves are the twins', Lina and Laura».

questions.q: The red cap is the writer's.
questions.explain_es: Verdadero. El narrador dice: «The red cap is mine!».

questions.q: The name on the sweater is J. ___.
questions.explain_es: El texto dice: «The name on it is J. Ruiz».

questions.q: Julián is in the classroom today.
questions.explain_es: Falso. El texto dice: «Julián Ruiz is not here today. He is at home».
«the red books are for Class B».

questions.q: The pencils are on the table.
questions.explain_es: Falso: «Your pencils are in the box».

listening.title: In a Clothes Shop in Cartagena

lines.text: Good afternoon. Welcome to Sol y Mar.
Hi. How much is this shirt?
That blue shirt is twenty-five dollars.
And how much are those shorts over there?
These white shorts? They are eighteen dollars.
OK. The shirt is for me, and the shorts are for my brother. His name is Nico.
Great. That is forty-three dollars, please.
Here you are. Thank you. Goodbye!
Thank you. Have a nice day!
Good morning! What is your name?
Good morning, teacher. My name is Mateo.
How do you spell that?
M, A, T, E, O.
Thank you. How old are you, Mateo?
I am eleven.
Where are you from?
I am from Pasto.
Is this your backpack?
No, it isn’t. My backpack is green. That black backpack is Lucía’s.
OK. What is your phone number?
It is three, one, five, four, zero, zero, two.
Great. Welcome to the class!
Nico, it is very cold today. Where is your jacket?
It is in my bedroom, Mom.
And your shoes?
My shoes are under the bed.
These socks are dirty. Whose socks are these?
They are Dad’s socks!
Oh! What day is it today?
It is Friday, the twentieth of June.
Friday! Your English class is at four o’clock.
Yes. My teacher is Miss Clark. She is very nice.
Good. Put on your jacket, please.

questions.explain_es: La vendedora dice: «That blue shirt is twenty-five dollars».
La vendedora dice: «That blue shirt is twenty-five dollars».
La vendedora dice: «They are eighteen dollars».

questions.q: The shorts are for the man's sister.
questions.explain_es: Falso. El cliente dice: «the shorts are for my brother».
El cliente dice: «His name is Nico».

questions.q: How much is it in total?
questions.explain_es: La vendedora dice: «That is forty-three dollars, please».

questions.q: The shop is called Sol y Mar.
questions.explain_es: Verdadero. La vendedora dice: «Welcome to Sol y Mar».

questions.q: The shirt is for the man.
questions.explain_es: Verdadero. El cliente dice: «The shirt is for me».

questions.q: What time of day is it?

questions.explain_es: Three, one, five, four, zero, zero, two.

questions.q: At the end the teacher says: «___ to the class!»
The English class is at ___ o’clock.
Nico’s English teacher is Miss Clark.

writing.prompt: What are you wearing today? Describe your clothes and the clothes of a friend or a person in your family. Say the colours and use 's (for example, my sister's bag).
writing.prompt_es: Describe la ropa que llevas hoy y la de un amigo o familiar, con colores y el posesivo 's.
criteria: Use be + wearing: I am wearing… / She is wearing…
Name at least four clothes with their colours.
Use a possessive adjective (my, his, her).
writing.model: Today I am wearing blue jeans, a white T-shirt and black sneakers. This is my sister, Paula. She is wearing a yellow dress. Her jacket is red. The green bag is my mom's.

prompts.text: Talk about two people in your family. Say their names, how old they are and where they are from. Spell one of the names.
prompts.text_es: Habla de dos personas de tu familia: nombre, edad y de dónde son. Deletrea uno de los nombres.
tips: This is my… His / Her name is…

prompts.text: Describe what you are wearing today, with colours. Then describe what a person near you is wearing.
prompts.text_es: Describe la ropa que llevas hoy, con colores, y la de una persona cerca de ti.

prompts.text: Role-play: you find a phone, a bag and some keys in your classroom. Ask who the owners are with Whose, and answer with 's, mine or yours.
prompts.text_es: Juego de roles: encuentras un celular, un bolso y unas llaves en el salón. Pregunta de quién son con Whose y responde con 's, mine o yours.
